tagline: A scored quiz that branches to a personalized result
verdictSummary: A quiz that assigns points per answer and branches to a personalized result based on the total score — involve.me's actual interactive-quiz mechanic — is a real weekend build, genuinely similar arithmetic to this catalogue's Paperform price-calculator entry but branching on a total score rather than displaying a running price.
coreLoopDIY: Build a multi-question quiz where each answer option is assigned points, sum the points as the visitor answers, and show one of several pre-written result pages based on which score range the total falls into.
whatYouLose: a large template library of pre-built quiz formats
advanced analytics on drop-off per question
whyPeopleStillPay: Scoring and branching to a result is simple arithmetic; a library of proven quiz templates and integrations with the marketing tools people actually use to follow up on leads is the ongoing product surface.
prompt: Build an interactive scored quiz tool — involve.me's actual mechanic, distinct from this catalogue's Paperform entry, which calculates a running price rather than branching to a result. Use Next.js/TypeScript with SQLite. In the quiz builder, let the creator write multiple-choice questions where each answer option is assigned a point value. As a visitor answers, sum the points client-side for a responsive feel, then validate the total server-side on submission — never trust a client-reported score for anything that matters. Define result tiers: score ranges each mapped to a pre-written result page (title, description, optional call-to-action link). Show the visitor their matching result immediately after the last question. Capture an optional email address before revealing the result, a common lead-generation pattern, and store the visitor's answers, score, and email in SQLite. Notify the quiz owner of new leads via a transactional email provider. Do not build a large template library, marketing-tool integrations, or A/B testing of quiz variants — those are out of scope; this is one scored quiz with configurable results, nothing more. Requires a domain and a transactional email provider; no other external service needed.

faq.q: How is this different from the Paperform build in this catalogue?
faq.a: Paperform's build calculates a running price total; this one sums points to branch into one of several pre-written result pages, a genuinely different interaction even though the underlying arithmetic is similar.

faq.q: Is the score calculated safely, or can someone cheat it?
faq.a: The total is validated server-side on submission, not trusted from the client, so someone can't just edit the page to force a specific result.

faq.q: Can I build multiple different quizzes?
faq.a: Yes, each with its own questions, point values, and result tiers — but there's no shared template library to start from, unlike involve.me's.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: A domain plus a transactional email provider's free tier — typically nothing beyond what you already pay for the domain.
